football_evidence.question: Can Tulane’s pass rush get to Owen McCown?
football_evidence.assessment: Most of the 2.8-point difference traces to home field (engine constant) (about 1.1 points), which the closing market has historically priced differently. That explains the gap; it does not make either number a bet.
supporting: When UTSA has the ball (the red zone): UTSA’s offense succeeds on 42.9% of its red-zone plays, and Tulane’s defense allows success on 30.4% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Tulane’s receivers No. 73 nationally and UTSA’s No. 121.
contradicting: When Tulane has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Tulane’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.3% of its dropbacks, and UTSA’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Tulane has the ball (early downs): Tulane’s offense succeeds on 33.9% of its first- and second-down plays, and UTSA’s defense allows success on 41.7% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.7%).

When UTSA has the ball (big plays on the ground): UTSA’s offense turns 8.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Tulane’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
In his last two games (Southern Miss and Army), Semonza averaged 5.8 yards per attempt, against 7.5 in his three games before that.
quarterbacks: Kadin Semonza has completed 64 of 119 passes (53.8%) for 808 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for Tulane, and has been sacked on 13 of 132 dropbacks.
Trace Johnson has completed 13 of 26 passes (50.0%) for 200 yards, 7.7 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in two games for Tulane, and has been sacked on 1 of 27 dropbacks.
Owen McCown has completed 151 of 218 passes (69.3%) for 1,565 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in seven games for UTSA, and has been sacked on 9 of 227 dropbacks.
